# ag-shared Sync Log

Migration log for `external/ag-shared/` changes. Each entry documents what changed and what companion actions consuming repos need to perform when syncing.

Newest entries first. Generated by `/ag-shared-sync-log`.

---

## 2026-08-10 -- PR previews stop publishing source maps, and stop resurrecting cleaned-up directories

**Branch:** `review-pr-snapshot-report-publishing-ab2d`

### Changes

- **[github]** `pr-preview-publish`: new `include_source_maps` input, **default `false`** — a sibling `<file>.map` is no longer published unless a caller opts in. Behaviour change for existing callers. Measured on ag-charts, source maps were 897 MB of a 1,155 MB Pages site (~12 MB of each ~16 MB preview). GitHub Pages rebuilds the whole site on every push to the publish branch and its branch builds are single-flight, so that weight is paid by every PR on every deploy; it was the main driver of deploy latency.
- **[github]** `pr-preview-publish`: new `skip_when_closed` input, **default `true`** — re-reads PR state immediately before pushing and skips the publish when the PR is already closed or merged. Fails open (publishes) when state cannot be read, so a job without `pull-requests` scope keeps working. Fixes previews being orphaned forever when a CI run still in flight at merge time republished `pr-<N>/` minutes after close-time cleanup removed it.
- **[github]** `pr-preview-lib/gh-pages-commit.sh`: `TARGET_PREFIX` now accepts a whitespace-separated list of paths in `MODE=remove`, so a bulk sweep lands as one push (one Pages build) rather than one push per path. `MODE=sync` still requires exactly one prefix and errors otherwise. Paths are validated against absolute, `.`, `..` and traversal entries before `rm -rf` runs. Paths must not contain whitespace.
- **[github]** `pr-preview-janitor`: new composite action. Sweeps a publish branch for previews belonging to closed PRs and for `.map` files under `pr-*/`, removing everything it finds in one push. Inputs: `publish_branch`, `dry_run`, `purge_source_maps`, `github_token`; outputs `paths` and `count`. Aborts rather than sweeping if the branch cannot be listed, and keeps any preview whose PR state cannot be read. This is what actually closes the publish-after-cleanup race; `skip_when_closed` only narrows it.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Review callers of `pr-preview-publish` in `.github/workflows/`: any that relied on source maps being published must now pass `include_source_maps: true`.
- [ ] Confirm jobs calling `pr-preview-publish` grant `pull-requests: read` (or `write`), otherwise `skip_when_closed` fails open and logs a warning on every publish.
- [ ] Adopt the janitor by copying ag-charts' `.github/workflows/gh-pages-janitor.yml` — a ~50-line caller (schedule, `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run`, `contents: write` + `pull-requests: read`, checkout, then the action). The workflow has to live in each repo's `.github/workflows/`; the sweep itself does not.
- [ ] After adopting, run it once with `dry_run: true` and check the job summary before letting it sweep for real — repos that have never pruned may have a large backlog.
- [ ] Set `purge_source_maps: false` in any repo that passes `include_source_maps: true` to `pr-preview-publish`, otherwise the sweep deletes what the publish just wrote.
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/verify-rulesync.sh`

### Notes

Publishes overlay rather than replace, so source maps already on the publish branch persist until their PR closes — dropping them from future publishes does not reclaim the existing ones. Reclaiming those needs an explicit sweep.

`skip_when_closed` narrows the publish-after-cleanup race to the seconds between the state check and the push; it does not close it. A periodic sweep is what guarantees convergence.

## 2026-08-03 -- Claude Code cloud sessions start with the toolchain, dependencies and skills in place

**Branch:** `goal-allow-claude-code-web-e6d4`

### Changes

- **[scripts/install-for-cloud/cloud-setup.sh]** New. The script a cloud environment's **Setup script** field runs (via a small locator snippet pasted at `claude.ai/code`), once per environment and before Claude Code launches: pins node to `.nvmrc` through nvm, installs `yarn@1` and `nx` globally, registers the plugin marketplaces and installs the plugins named in `.claude/settings.json` through the `claude plugin` CLI, runs `yarn install --ignore-scripts` (the slow, cacheable part — a full install needs ~9 min and the cap is ~5), and seeds `/opt/ag-cloud` with `node_modules` keyed to the `yarn.lock` hash, marked `unscripted`, plus the resolved node bin path. It only caches a tree from an install that finished. Every step is best-effort and the script always exits 0, because a non-zero exit fails session creation.
- **[scripts/install-for-cloud/install-for-cloud.sh]** In cloud mode it now exports the node recorded by `cloud-setup.sh` (into `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` and the profile, since the image's own node otherwise wins on PATH) and restores `node_modules` from the cache when the working tree arrives without it and the lockfile still matches. Restore tries reflink, then move, then hardlink, then plain copy — a hardlink copy of ag-charts' 2.3 GB / ~200k-file tree measured 78 s, so it cannot be the primary path. In a cloud session it never installs: it reports what is missing and names `finish-setup.sh`, and it clears install locks whose owning process is gone. Local and worktree behaviour is unchanged.
- **[scripts/install-for-cloud/finish-setup.sh]** New. Foreground completion step, needed once per session before any build, test or lint: takes a pid-stamped lock, runs `yarn install --prefer-offline` on the restored tree (~150 s measured, against ~534 s cold), refreshes the cache, then prints the doctor report. Needed because the ~5 minute setup cap cannot fit a full install (~9 min), a blocking SessionStart hook freezes the session, and a detached install does not outlive the session that spawned it. Per session rather than once per environment because each session is a fresh VM restored from the environment snapshot — verified from uptime against cache timestamps.
- **[scripts/install-for-cloud/wait-for-deps.sh]** Treats an install as in flight only while the process holding the lock is alive, and points at `finish-setup.sh` when nothing is running.
- **[scripts/install-for-cloud/cloud-doctor.sh]** New. Session readiness report: toolchain versions against `.nvmrc`, `node_modules` integrity, cache state, `.claude/settings.json` and rules, marketplace **registration** (not just a clone on disk), and the five canary skills. Prints `READY` or the specific gaps; safe to run locally.
- **[docs/claude-code-cloud-sessions.md]** New. The setup-script snippet to paste, the required second repository, what runs at environment build vs per session, why `.claude/settings.json` has to be committed, and the known limitations (no `.mcp.json`, generated rules/skills, private marketplace, unauthenticated setup phase, launch-time skill enumeration, Playwright, VM memory).

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Un-ignore the rendered Claude Code settings so cloud sessions get hooks and plugins at all. In `.gitignore`, replace `/.claude/` with `/.claude/*` plus `!/.claude/settings.json`, then commit `.claude/settings.json`. Confirm the render is reproducible first: `AG_DEV_PROMPTS_REF=canary ./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh --postinstall` must leave the file unchanged, otherwise every `yarn` dirties the tree.
- [ ] Add `.claude/settings.json` to `.prettierignore` in the same change. Once the file is tracked, prettier reformats it and the next `yarn` renders it straight back — `nx format:check` and postinstall flip it in turn, and one of them is always failing. The template injects the marketplace `ref` inline via sed, which is why the render is not prettier-shaped to begin with.
- [ ] Add the setup script to each cloud environment at `claude.ai/code` (and to the organization-shared environment, if the team uses one) using the snippet in `docs/claude-code-cloud-sessions.md`. Nothing in the repo can do this — the field lives in the environment dialog.
- [ ] Attach `ag-grid/ag-dev-prompts` to the session as a second repository. The setup phase has no GitHub credentials, so the private marketplace can only be registered from that local checkout. Note this also moves the session's working directory to the parent of the repos.
- [ ] Verify with `cd /home/user/<repo> && bash external/ag-shared/scripts/install-for-cloud/cloud-doctor.sh` in a cloud session, and check the setup log for a failed marketplace registration.
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`

### Notes

Before this, a cloud session in an AG repo was structurally unable to bootstrap itself. Only files in the clone reach the session, `/.claude/` was ignored wholesale, and `.claude/settings.json` is generated by postinstall — so the clone carried no SessionStart hook to trigger `yarn`, and no `enabledPlugins`/`extraKnownMarketplaces` to deliver skills. Nothing ran, and nothing was there to make anything run. Committing the rendered settings breaks that cycle; the setup script then covers the toolchain and dependencies, and the environment snapshot makes it a one-time cost per environment.

`ag-grid/ag-dev-prompts` is private, and cloud sessions reach GitHub through a proxy that scopes requests to the repositories attached to the session. Whether a marketplace clone of an unattached private repo succeeds is not documented either way, so the setup script attempts it explicitly (plain HTTPS, then `GH_TOKEN`, then SSH) and logs a clear warning on failure, and `cloud-doctor.sh` reports the missing marketplace and skills. That turns a silent "the skills are just not there" into a diagnosable line in the setup log.

`.claude/rules/` and `.claude/skills/` remain generated and ignored. They are present for the first session in an environment (written by the setup script's install before launch) and whenever the snapshot preserves the tree, but a session starting from a fresh clone regenerates them only after Claude Code has loaded its context. `CLAUDE.md` is committed, so the critical instructions always arrive.

## 2026-07-29 -- verify-rulesync fails a source rule that declares its scope under `paths:`

**Branch:** `b14.1.0`

### Changes

- **[scripts/setup-prompts/verify-rulesync.sh]** New `verify_source_frontmatter()` check, run from `main()` after `verify_content()`. It inspects only the frontmatter block of each `.rulesync/rules/*.md` and **errors** when the source declares `paths:`, because rulesync accepts `globs:` and *emits* `paths:` — a source file using the output key has its scope silently dropped and the rule is then injected into every conversation. It **warns** (does not fail) when a rule declares neither `globs:` nor `alwaysApply: true`, and when a rule has no frontmatter at all.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/verify-rulesync.sh` and fix any `uses 'paths:'` errors by renaming the key to `globs:` — the value becomes a YAML list. ag-charts had three: `api-contracts.md`, `entry-point-hygiene.md`, `module-support.md`.
- [ ] Review the new `declares neither 'globs:' nor 'alwaysApply: true'` warnings and confirm each such rule is genuinely meant to load in every conversation.
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`

### Notes

Content verification deliberately calls `strip_frontmatter` before every source↔output comparison, so it validates bodies only and this class of defect was structurally invisible to it. The three ag-charts rules had been generating `.claude/rules/*.md` with **no frontmatter at all** — and therefore no path restriction — while correctly-keyed siblings such as `series.md` generated `paths: ['**/series/**/*.ts']`. The three were being injected into every conversation in the repo regardless of the files under edit, at a cost of ~172 source lines (~9 KB) per conversation. The likely origin is someone copying the key from generated output back into a source file, which is silent in both directions.

The `paths:` case is an error rather than a warning because it is unambiguous — rulesync never accepts that key in a source file, so there is no legitimate use. The missing-key case is only a warning because an unrestricted rule can be deliberate. Consuming repos that vendor this script should expect the new check to fail loudly on first run if they carry the same defect; that failure is the point.

## 2026-07-28 -- Reconcile node_modules on an inexact cache restore under cache_mode:ro

**Branch:** `at/website-build-stale-node-modules`

### Changes

- **[github]** `setup-nx-core`: the `yarn_postinstall: no-install` path no longer requires `cache_mode: rw`. It now runs for both cache modes, and on an inexact `restore-keys` fallback it runs `yarn install --ci --prefer-offline` before the integrity check instead of nothing at all.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Review any job passing `cache_mode: ro` with `yarn_postinstall: no-install` — those jobs previously performed no install and no integrity check, and will now install on a cache-key miss (adds ~1-2 min on that path only).
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/verify-rulesync.sh`

### Notes

Fixes a silent-wrong-build race, not a hard failure. A job in `cache_mode: ro` whose exact `node_modules-<os>-<lockfile-hash>` key missed would restore an older tree via the `node_modules-<os>-` prefix fallback and build against it, so a dependency added in the same commit appeared as an unresolved import. In AG Charts this surfaced as `Website Build` failing with `Rollup failed to resolve import "@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu"` even though the dependency was correctly declared in both `package.json` and `yarn.lock`. It self-heals once any `rw` job saves a tree under the new hash, which makes it intermittent and easy to misread as a source error.

The old condition's third clause (`steps.cache_ro.outputs.cache-hit != 'false'`) was vacuous: `cache_ro` only runs under `cache_mode: ro`, so in the `rw` mode the same condition required, the step is skipped and its output is the empty string. It has been dropped rather than carried over.

## 2026-07-27 -- E2E shard timings are per-CI-event-type

**Branch:** `ci-fix/latest-0e9618c8-e2e-shard-timings`

### Changes

- **[scripts/shard/assign-e2e-shards.js]** Documentation only — no behaviour change. The regeneration notes previously said to aggregate "a recent full CI run", which does not distinguish a push run from a pull-request run. Where a workflow varies its framework matrix or snapshot capture by event type, the same spec file costs different amounts in each, so timings taken from one event type cannot plan shards for the other. The docstring now states that invariant, tells the reader to pick a run of the matching event type, and warns that `aggregate` silently skips artifacts with no `reports/` directory (those spec files then fall back to median weight). `aggregate`'s emitted `_readme` carries a short form of the same warning.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] None required — the script's inputs and output are unchanged, so consumers pick this up on the next sync.
- [ ] Recommended for any consumer that varies its E2E workload by event type: commit one timings file per event type and select it in the `--timings` argument. ag-charts now keeps `shard-timings.json` (push) alongside `shard-timings.pr.json` (pull request) and picks between them in `ci.yml`.

### Notes

- Prompted by an ag-charts `latest` CI failure (run 30282790699). Its committed timings had been regenerated from a PR-scoped run, which sweeps only the vanilla example variant with `AG_SCENE_SNAPSHOTS=diff`. On a push all six framework variants run with `AG_SCENE_SNAPSHOTS=all`, making every `generated/examples-*.spec.ts` cost ~10x its recorded duration while hand-written specs stayed accurate (measured medians: 10.48x and 1.00x). The bin-packer under-weighted the generated specs and overfilled the trailing bins — one shard was planned at 137s, ran 1765s of tests, and tripped the 15-minute step timeout with all 595 of its tests passing.

## 2026-07-27 -- PR-preview gh-pages publishing: push-retry instead of a global lock

**Branch:** `at/gh-pages-preview-push-retry`

### Changes

- **[github]** New shared script `github/actions/pr-preview-lib/gh-pages-commit.sh`. It clones the publish branch, applies one `pr-<N>/` subtree operation (`MODE=sync` overlays staged files, `MODE=remove` deletes the subtree), commits, and pushes inside a bounded retry loop: on a rejected push it refetches the branch tip, re-applies the operation, and pushes again. Because every writer only ever touches files under its own `pr-<N>/` prefix, diverged refs between concurrent writers never conflict, so a lock is no longer needed to serialise different PRs.
- **[github]** `github/actions/pr-preview-publish/action.yml`: dropped the `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3` dependency. It now stages the bundles into a flat dir and delegates the deploy to `gh-pages-commit.sh` (`MODE=sync`). Inputs are unchanged.
- **[github]** `github/actions/pr-preview-cleanup/action.yml`: replaced its bespoke clone/commit/single-retry with a call to `gh-pages-commit.sh` (`MODE=remove`). Inputs are unchanged; the branch-missing and subtree-absent no-op behaviours are preserved.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] None required for the actions themselves — inputs are unchanged, so consumers pick this up in place on the next sync.
- [ ] Recommended follow-up in each consuming repo's workflows: the global `pr-preview-gh-pages` concurrency group can be narrowed to a per-PR group (`pr-preview-gh-pages-<pr-number>`), so different PRs no longer serialise on gh-pages. The per-PR lock still matters — it stops a PR's publishers running concurrently with its own close-time cleanup, narrowing the window in which a late publish could re-create a removed `pr-<N>/` (job concurrency prevents overlap but not strict ordering, so it narrows rather than closes that window). Every job that publishes into the preview must join the group (in ag-charts that meant adding it to the previously-unlocked `snapshot_review` job). ag-charts applies this in `ci.yml` (`pr_preview`, `snapshot_review`) and `pr-cleanup.yml` (`gh_pages_cleanup`).

### Notes

- The retry loop was verified locally against a bare file:// remote: orphan first-publish, five concurrent writers to distinct prefixes (all land), remove mode, subtree-absent and branch-absent no-ops, and a forced single push-rejection that recovers on retry.
- `PUBLISH_REMOTE` is a test-only seam that overrides the derived `github.com` remote; production callers never set it.

## 2026-07-21 -- Fix dropped node_modules cache save in setup-nx-core

**Branch:** `latest` (working change)

### Changes

- **[github]** `github/actions/setup-nx-core/action.yml`: split the `rw` node_modules cache into an explicit `actions/cache/restore@v4` + `actions/cache/save@v4` (save runs after `yarn install`, only on a non-exact restore). Previously a single `actions/cache@v4` relied on its post-save hook, whose `path` is `${{ inputs.node_modules_paths }}` — but expression contexts are lost in post steps of nested composite actions (actions/runner#2009). Since #14378 (2026-07-09) nested this action under the `setup-nx` wrapper, `path` resolved empty at post time and the save was silently dropped (`Input required and not supplied: path`); the Nx cache kept saving only because its `path` is a literal. Every job fell back to a stale restore-key cache from 2026-07-05 and reinstalled dependencies (~3 min) on each run.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Sync the ag-shared subrepo, then verify a `latest` CI run emits `Cache saved with key: node_modules-Linux-<current-hash>` in the "Initialise Workflow" job and that subsequent runs report `EXACT_CACHE_HIT: true`.
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/verify-rulesync.sh`

### Notes

Independent of this fix, the cache key still hashes every workspace `package.json`, so version-bump merges keep minting new hashes — but with saving restored, each new hash persists once on `latest` and is then shared to PRs, which is the intended behaviour.

## 2026-07-13 -- Recycle batch-worker pool on heap growth

**Branch:** `at/thumbnail-generation-memory`

### Changes

- **[scripts/plugin-utils/executors-utils.ts]** `batchWorkerExecutor` now passes `maxMemoryLimitBeforeRecycle` to its Tinypool, recycling a pooled child-process worker once its heap crosses a ceiling (default 1GiB, overridable via `NX_WORKER_RECYCLE_HEAP_BYTES`). Chart-thumbnail render workers retain memory that GC cannot reclaim (~90MB per example); on a constrained CI runner the reused workers grew until the runner exhausted memory and stalled at the batch tail. Recycling bounds per-worker memory regardless of the underlying retention. Applies to every consumer of `batchWorkerExecutor` (example-file and thumbnail generation).

### Migration Actions

- [ ] None — consumed in place; takes effect on next sync. Optionally set `NX_WORKER_RECYCLE_HEAP_BYTES` in a repo's CI env to tune the ceiling.

### Notes

- Requires `tinypool` ≥ the version exposing `maxMemoryLimitBeforeRecycle` (2.1.0 in ag-charts). The option is ignored when `isolateWorkers` is set.

## 2026-06-10 -- Batched Claude formatting hooks (track / Stop-format / commit-gate)

**Branch:** `ajt/claude-format-hooks`
**Commits:** `d2ac0d251d..8a86d6b137` (2 commits)

### Changes

- **[scripts/claude-hooks]** New directory of Claude Code hook scripts: `track-edit.sh` (PostToolUse — records edited file paths to a per-session list under `$TMPDIR`), `format-tracked.sh` (Stop — one batched `nx format` per turn, clears the list on success, surfaces parse errors), `precommit-check.sh` (PreToolUse Bash — read-only gate that denies a `git commit` whose staged blobs are not prettier-formatted), plus `_common.sh` helpers and a README.
- **[settings]** `.claude-settings.template.json`: replaced the per-edit `PostToolUse` `nx format --files` hook with the three hooks above (`PostToolUse` → track, `Stop` → format, `PreToolUse` Bash → commit gate).

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh` to regenerate `.claude/settings.json` from the template.
- [ ] Restart Claude Code / your IDE so the new hooks load. `setup-prompts` overwrites `.claude/settings.json`, so any IDE-injected hooks are re-applied on restart.
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/verify-rulesync.sh`.

### Notes

Replaces ~2.4–3.8s of per-edit `nx format` latency (~4 hrs/month of serialised hook time) with one batched format per turn plus a commit-time check. The commit gate verifies the staged index blob with the repo's own prettier — byte-identical to `nx format`, honouring `.prettierignore` — and never mutates files. Files `nx format` cannot map to a project (root configs) remain un-auto-formatted, as before.

## 2026-06-08 -- Shared JIRA-pipeline glue: install-ag-dev-prompts + pr-preview publish/cleanup

**Branch:** `feat/jira-pipeline-shared-actions`
**Ticket:** AG-17085 (JIRA/GHA agent-pipeline rollout) / ag-grid onboarding

### Changes

- **[github/actions/install-ag-dev-prompts/action.yml]** New composite action. Installs the private `@ag-grid/dev-prompts` npm package from GitHub Packages into `$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.ag-dev-prompts` so the pipeline *engine* actions shipped inside it (`jira-pipeline`, `jira-resume-preflight`, `jira-ci-success-handler`, `jira-pr-plnkr`, …) can be consumed via local-path `uses:`. Inputs: `channel` (npm dist-tag — `latest`/`canary`), `github-token` (default `github.token`), optional `node-version` override. Defaults to the consumer repo's root `package.json` via `node-version-file` so the one action fits every repo. Generalised from ag-charts' repo-local `.github/actions/install-ag-dev-prompts` (which had `node-version: '20'` hardcoded). The engine actions themselves stay on the channel-pinned npm package — only this install glue is shared.
- **[github/actions/pr-preview-publish/action.yml]** New composite action. Stages caller-resolved UMD bundle file paths (plus any sibling `<file>.map`) under `pr-<N>/`, writes `_publish/.nojekyll`, and deploys to `gh-pages` via `peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3` (`keep_files: true`). Skips cleanly (warning, not error) when no listed bundle exists (tooling-only PRs). Inputs: `pr_number`, `files` (newline-separated), `github_token`, `publish_branch` (default `gh-pages`). The product-specific `build:umd`, artifact handoff, and live-test PR comment stay in each repo's `ci.yml` (served URL differs per repo). Caller owns the `pr-preview-gh-pages` job concurrency group.
- **[github/actions/pr-preview-cleanup/action.yml]** New composite action. Removes a PR's `pr-<N>/` directory from `gh-pages` on PR close (`git rm` + commit + push with rebase-retry). Caller checks out `gh-pages` first with workflow-level `continue-on-error` (the first-run guard — `continue-on-error` is unsupported on steps inside composite actions) and gates the action call on it. Inputs: `pr_number`, `publish_branch` (default `gh-pages`).

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Pull ag-shared in each consumer repo (`yarn subrepo pull ag-shared`). The three new actions arrive automatically.
- [ ] **ag-charts (per-repo follow-up):** migrate `.github/workflows/jira-agent-pipeline.yml` to `uses: ./external/ag-shared/github/actions/install-ag-dev-prompts`; replace the `ci.yml` `pr_preview` stage+deploy steps with `pr-preview-publish`; replace the `pr-cleanup.yml` `gh_pages_cleanup` remove step with `pr-preview-cleanup`; delete the now-redundant `.github/actions/install-ag-dev-prompts/`. Behaviour must be unchanged (same `…/ag-charts/pr-<N>/…` URLs).

## 2026-04-23 -- Worktree create fast path

**Branch:** `ajt/worktree-create-fast-path`
**Ticket:** none

### Changes

- **[scripts/setup-worktree/preinstall-worktree.sh]**
    -   `clone_directory()` uses a single `clonefile(2)` syscall on macOS for whole-tree O(1) COW — ~8× faster than `cp -cR` for large node_modules / .nx trees. Falls back to `cp -cR` then `rsync` on non-macOS or when the destination already exists.
    -   `REPO_ROOT` prefers `$PWD` when it contains a `package.json`, falling back to the `BASH_SOURCE`-derived path. Fixes mode misdetection when the script is invoked from a worktree via the `external/ag-shared` symlink (previous behaviour resolved back to the main repo and reported `Mode: local`).
    -   New `hash_workspace_layout()` + `workspace_layouts_match()` — compares glob-resolved workspace `package.json` sets between source and worktree. Catches workspace additions that leave `yarn.lock` untouched.
    -   New `source_has_all_plugin_dists()` — iterates `plugins/*/project.json`, and for each plugin with a `build` target, requires a corresponding source `dist/`. Refuses the fast path if any is missing, so a `yarn nx clean`ed source never produces a silent fast-path skip of plugin outputs.
    -   New `try_cow_clone_plugin_dists()` — COW-clones the gitignored `plugins/*/dist` outputs (redundant on macOS where the top-level clone already recurses; belt-and-braces for the `rsync` fallback).
    -   Writes `node_modules/.ag-worktree-fast-path-ok` marker only when lockfile parity, workspace topology, plugin-dist completeness, and every COW clone succeed. `clear_fast_path_marker` wipes it on every run so stale markers cannot persist.
- **[scripts/setup-worktree/claude-worktree-create.sh]**
    -   Invokes `preinstall-worktree.sh` directly against the worktree instead of relying on `yarn install` as the driver.
    -   Fast path (marker present): skips `yarn install` and runs `AG_WORKTREE_FAST_PATH=1 yarn run postinstall`. Expensive postinstall steps self-skip via the env var; cheap idempotent steps (`setup-git-hooks`, `setup-prompts`) still run. Future postinstall steps run by default unless the consumer repo explicitly gates them.
    -   Slow path (marker absent): runs `yarn install --offline --frozen-lockfile` with `AG_PREINSTALL_ACTIVE=1` so the preinstall hook does not duplicate the COW work. Falls back to `--prefer-offline` if the offline path fails.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Next `yarn subrepo pull ag-shared` picks up the script changes automatically; no per-repo script action.
- [ ] **Optional — to realise the full speedup in consuming repos**, gate expensive postinstall steps on `AG_WORKTREE_FAST_PATH=1` in the consumer's `package.json`. Example:
    ```json
    "postinstall:plugin-build": "[ \"$AG_WORKTREE_FAST_PATH\" = \"1\" ] || nx run-many -p tag:plugin -t build"
    ```
    Candidates are any postinstall step that recreates state the COW clone has already produced: plugin builds, Nx workspace-data wipes/daemon restarts, patch re-application. Leave idempotent/cheap steps (git hooks, prompts staging) ungated. Not applying the gates is safe — those steps simply run redundantly on the fast path, narrowing the saving but producing a correct state.
- [ ] On macOS, verify that `python3` is available on `PATH` — the new `clone_directory()` fast path shells out to it once for the `clonefile(2)` syscall. Falls back to `cp -cR` if absent, so no action required unless you want the fastest path.

### Notes

On ag-charts the hook time drops from ~100s to ~14–20s for a clean worktree from `latest` (node_modules parity, no source edits). Breakdown: `clonefile(2)` trims the `cp -cR` cost from ~36s to ~4s for `node_modules`; skipping `postinstall:plugin-build` trims another ~22s (the cost comes from `postinstall:nx-daemon-reset-metadata` wiping `.nx/workspace-data/` and forcing a cold daemon startup, not from the plugin `tsc` runs themselves); skipping `yarn install`'s validation trims ~8–10s.

See `ag-grid/ag-charts#6654` for the original change and measurements.

## 2026-04-21 -- stage.py: stale cleanup preserves tracked local files

**Branch:** `AG-17098/stage-preserve-tracked`
**Ticket:** AG-17098

### Changes

- **[scripts/rulesync-fetch]** `stage.py` stale-cleanup pass now skips paths that git tracks. Previous behaviour would delete any file whose name appears in the full unfiltered manifest but not in the filtered staged set — which includes genuine local rules that happen to share a filename with a plugin-contributed guide. New `_tracked_files()` helper runs `git ls-files .rulesync/` and the cleanup loop logs `keeping tracked <path> (not a stage-leftover)` for matches, preserving the file on disk.
- Handles non-git environments gracefully: if `git` fails (e.g. sandbox without a repo), returns an empty set — falls back to prior behaviour for ad-hoc runs.

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Next `yarn subrepo pull ag-shared` picks this up automatically; no per-repo action.
- [ ] If any developer's local `.rulesync/rules/*.md` was deleted by the previous stage.py run, restore from git: `git restore .rulesync/rules/<name>.md`.

### Notes

Caught during the ag-grid consumer-repo migration (ag-grid/ag-grid#13576). ag-grid tracks a `.rulesync/rules/benchmarks.md` / `testing.md` / `examples.md` / `docs-pages.md` — ag-grid-specific content. The ag-charts plugin ships guides with the same filenames. After the product filter landed (ag-grid/ag-shared#5), the ag-charts files stopped staging, so stale-cleanup saw them as removable — and deleted the tracked ag-grid versions. This fix scopes stale-cleanup to files not under git control, keeping local content authoritative.

## 2026-04-21 -- stage.py: product-scope plugin staging

**Branch:** `AG-17098/product-filter-stage`
**Ticket:** AG-17098

### Changes

- **[scripts/rulesync-fetch]** `stage.py` now filters the plugin-assignments manifest by product before staging into `.rulesync/`. `PRODUCT_PLUGINS = {ag-charts, ag-grid, ag-studio}`; generic plugins (`ag-core`, `ag-prodeng`) always stage; a product plugin stages iff its name matches the current repo's product. Product detection mirrors `setup-prompts.sh copy_extra_configs`: `$AG_PRODUCT` env var first, falling back to the workspace root's `package.json` `.name` field. Fails loudly if the name is not one of the known products.
- **[scripts/rulesync-fetch]** `stage()` now performs a stale-cleanup pass: after staging, it computes the full-manifest staging set and removes from `.rulesync/{skills,subagents,commands,rules}/` anything in the full set that isn't in the filtered set. Catches other-product content left over from previous runs (pre-filter or after a product switch).
- **[scripts/rulesync-fetch]** `list_staged()` gained `filter_by_product` kwarg (default True); the `--list` CLI honours the filter so `setup-prompts.sh` surfaces only the consuming product's staged paths. Internal helper `_stageable_paths(plugins)` factored out and reused by both the stale-cleanup diff and `list_staged()`.

### Migration Actions

Per consuming repo on next `yarn subrepo pull ag-shared`:

- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`. The stale-cleanup pass will drop any other-product content previously staged into `.rulesync/skills/`, `.rulesync/subagents/`, etc. (e.g. in the ag-grid checkout, ag-charts plugin items land for removal). Expect a one-time chunky diff in the follow-up commit.
- [ ] Restart any running Claude Code session — no behaviour change on the Claude side (it reads plugins directly), but Cursor / Codex / Gemini / AGENTS.md will stop seeing other-product items.

### Notes

Closes the follow-up flagged on ag-grid/ag-grid#13576. Before this change, `stage.py` copied every plugin's content from the manifest regardless of the consuming product — for Claude this was harmless (targets exclude `claudecode`), but non-Claude tools in an ag-grid checkout surfaced ag-charts-specific skills/agents/commands as first-class options, and vice versa.

The filter keys on the same workspace `package.json` `.name` field already used by `scripts/sonar/sync-sonar-issues.ts` and `setup-prompts.sh`, so there's one authoritative product source across the tooling.

## 2026-04-21 -- Templatise `.claude-settings.json` for per-product `enabledPlugins`

**Branch:** `AG-17098/templatise-claude-settings`
**Ticket:** AG-17098

### Changes

- **[settings]** `.claude-settings.json` replaced by `.claude-settings.template.json`. The `enabledPlugins` block now contains a `${PRODUCT}@ag-dev` placeholder alongside the always-on `ag-core@ag-dev` and `ag-prodeng@ag-dev` entries. Rendered to `.claude/settings.json` (real file, not symlink) by `setup-prompts.sh`.
- **[scripts/setup-prompts]** `copy_extra_configs` in `setup-prompts.sh` now renders the template via `sed` substitution. Product identifier is read from `$AG_PRODUCT` env var first, falling back to the workspace root's `package.json` `name` field — the same detection source `scripts/sonar/sync-sonar-issues.ts` already uses. Fails loudly if the detected name is not one of `ag-charts | ag-grid | ag-studio`. Stale symlinks at the destination are replaced with a real file atomically.
- **[scripts/sync-to-plugin]** `sync-to-plugin.sh` `EXCLUDE_FILES` list updated to exclude the new template filename.
- **[.claude-plugin]** `plugin-assignments.json` `excludedFromPlugin` note updated to mention the new template filename.

### Migration Actions

Per consuming repo (ag-charts first, then ag-grid and ag-studio once their rollouts begin):

- [ ] `yarn subrepo pull ag-shared`. No new marker file needed — the workspace root `package.json` `name` is authoritative (already `ag-charts` / `ag-grid` / `ag-studio`).
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`. Confirm `.claude/settings.json` is a real file (not a symlink) and contains the correct `${PRODUCT}@ag-dev: true` entry for this repo's product.
- [ ] Restart any running Claude Code session so the rendered settings take effect.
- [ ] No `.gitignore` change needed — the repo root `.claude/` directory is already gitignored in all three consuming repos.

### Notes

This change unblocks AG-17098 (ag-grid + ag-studio rollout). Before this, `.claude-settings.json` hardcoded `ag-charts@ag-dev: true`, forcing divergence if ag-grid or ag-studio pulled the subrepo. The template + renderer keeps the shared file as the single source of truth while letting each consumer pick its product plugin deterministically.

Detection uses `package.json` `name` because it is already the product-identification source elsewhere in ag-shared tooling (`scripts/sonar/sync-sonar-issues.ts` `PRODUCT_SONAR_KEYS`). Using the same convention here avoids adding a redundant marker file and removes any risk of the two sources drifting.

The substitution is a simple `sed "s|\${PRODUCT}|<name>|g"`. Product names are alphanumeric + hyphen only so there are no escaping concerns. The `.claude-settings.template.json` file is not valid JSON as-is (the placeholder is in a key position); editors may flag it — that's expected.

Prompted by a reproducible failure on a dev machine with no GitHub-registered SSH key but working `gh` auth. Tokens are never persisted to `.git/config`; they are passed via `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic …` for the single invocation only.

```markdown
## Tooling Health Check

On the **first response** of a conversation, verify that project skills are available by checking the system-reminder skill list. If **any** of the canary skills are missing, display a one-time warning before doing anything else. Do not repeat the warning on subsequent responses.

**Canary skills:** `example`, `dev-server`, `debug`, `git-conventions`, `jira`, `simplify`

**Warning to display (if any canary skill is missing):**

> **Agentic tooling is not initialised.** Expected skills (example, dev-server, debug, git-conventions, jira, simplify) are missing or incomplete. Run `yarn` from the repository root to set up AI tooling configuration, then restart your session. If you are in a worktree, ensure you ran `yarn` in the worktree directory (not just the main checkout).

Continue assisting the user after displaying the warning.
```

### Changes

- **[prompts/skills]** Added `rulesync` skill to replace the `rulesync` guide — comprehensive configuration reference for `.rulesync/` directory management
- **[prompts/guides]** Removed `rulesync.md` guide (superseded by the `rulesync` skill)
- **[prompts/skills]** Optimised `dev-server` skill — added multi-repo URL table, troubleshooting section, removed redundant `_dev-server-core.md` partial
- **[prompts/skills]** Optimised `plunker` skill — extracted CSS into `assets/ag-example-styles.css`, slimmed guide, improved description
- **[prompts/skills]** Enhanced `git-conventions` skill — expanded description for better auto-triggering, added PR base branch guidance
- **[prompts/skills]** Enhanced `pr-create` skill — improved PR creation guidelines
- **[prompts/config]** Added `WorktreeCreate` and `WorktreeRemove` hooks to `.claude-settings.json` for automated worktree lifecycle management
- **[scripts/setup-prompts]** Updated `verify-rulesync.sh` to include files in skill subdirectories (e.g. `assets/`) in the expected inventory
- **[scripts]** Added `scripts/setup-worktree/claude-worktree-create.sh` and `claude-worktree-remove.sh` for Claude Code worktree lifecycle

### Migration Actions

- [ ] Remove `.rulesync/rules/rulesync.md` file symlink (target guide was deleted)
- [ ] Add `.rulesync/skills/rulesync` directory symlink -> `../../external/ag-shared/prompts/skills/rulesync/`
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/setup-prompts.sh`
- [ ] Run `./external/ag-shared/scripts/setup-prompts/verify-rulesync.sh`

### Post-Migration Verification

- [ ] Confirm `/rulesync` skill is available (type `/rulesync help` in Claude Code)
- [ ] Confirm the old rulesync rule no longer loads (check `.claude/rules/` for stale `rulesync.md`)
- [ ] Test worktree creation: run `/worktree <branch-name>` in Claude Code and verify the hook creates the worktree under `~/.worktrees/<repo>/`
- [ ] Test worktree removal: exit the worktree session and verify cleanup runs without errors
- [ ] Verify `dev-server` skill still triggers correctly (`/dev-server help`)

### Notes

The `rulesync` guide-to-skill migration is a structural change: consuming repos that had a `.rulesync/rules/rulesync.md` file symlink pointing to `../../external/ag-shared/prompts/guides/rulesync.md` must remove it (the target no longer exists) and add a directory symlink at `.rulesync/skills/rulesync` instead. The new worktree hook scripts (`scripts/setup-worktree/`) are referenced from `.claude-settings.json` and do not need `.rulesync/` symlinks.
